Each of Mars' moons will give a force on the scale of around 10^14-15 each. They are however on two completely different orbits, giving a very variable force. With Mars having lower gravity as well, the forces will have a slightly larger effect than on Earth, but not too noticable.

The difference in orbits will cause the tides to run at very varying times on a very different schedule to that of the earth. I'd say tides are likely to be experienced on Mars.
